   587→    def build_gui_context(
   588→        self,
   589→        context: dict[str, str],
   590→        project_overrides: dict[str, str],
   591→    ) -> dict[str, str]:
   592→        """Build context specific to the GUI toolkit."""
   593→        bootstraps = get_gui_bootstraps()
   594→        bootstrap_options = self._gui_bootstrap_choices(bootstraps)
   595→
   596→        # Map the override value to the annotated override value so we can use it with self.select_option
   597→        # If a user specifies the override value PySide6, then we want it to be mapped to the annotated value
   598→        # "PySide6       (does not support iOS/Android deployment)"
   599→        # since that is the option presented to the user. To accomplish this, we map the bootstrap classes
   600→        # to their annotated names and do a reverse lookup from the override bootstrap class to the annotated name.
   601→        #
   602→        # We do it this way to ensure consistent prompting for the user.
   603→        if bootstrap_override := project_overrides.pop("bootstrap", None):
   604→            reverse_lookup = {v: k for k, v in bootstrap_options.items()}
   605→            if self.validate_selection_override(bootstraps.keys(), bootstrap_override):
   606→                bootstrap_override = reverse_lookup[bootstraps[bootstrap_override]]
   607→
   608→        selected_bootstrap = self.select_option(
   609→            intro=(
   610→                "What GUI toolkit do you want to use for this project?\n"
   611→                "\n"
   612→                "Additional GUI bootstraps are available; visit "
   613→                "https://beeware.org/bee/briefcase-bootstraps "
   614→                "for a full list of known GUI bootstraps."
   615→            ),
   616→            variable="GUI Framework",
   617→            default=None,
   618→            options=bootstrap_options.keys(),
   619→            override_value=bootstrap_override,
   620→        )
   621→        bootstrap_class = bootstrap_options[selected_bootstrap]
   622→
   623→        gui_context = {}
   624→
   625→        if bootstrap_class is not None:
   626→            bootstrap: BaseGuiBootstrap = bootstrap_class(context=context)
   627→
   628→            # Iterate over the Bootstrap interface to build the context.
   629→            # Returning ``None`` is a special case that means the field should not be
   630→            # included in the context and instead deferred to the template default.
   631→
   632→            if hasattr(bootstrap, "extra_context"):
   633→                if (additional_context := bootstrap.extra_context()) is not None:
   634→                    gui_context.update(additional_context)
   635→
   636→            for context_field in bootstrap.fields:
   637→                if (context_value := getattr(bootstrap, context_field)()) is not None:
   638→                    gui_context[context_field] = context_value
   639→
   640→        return gui_context

   642→    def _gui_bootstrap_choices(self, bootstraps):
   643→        """Construct the list of available GUI bootstraps to display to the user."""
   644→        # Sort the options alphabetically first
   645→        ordered = OrderedDict(sorted(bootstraps.items()))
   646→
   647→        # Ensure the first 5 options are: Toga, PySide6, Pygame
   648→        ordered.move_to_end("Pygame", last=False)
   649→        ordered.move_to_end("PySide6", last=False)
   650→        ordered.move_to_end("Toga", last=False)
   651→
   652→        # Option None should always be last
   653→        ordered["None"] = None
   654→        ordered.move_to_end("None")
   655→
   656→        # Construct the bootstrap options as they should be presented to users.
   657→        # The name of the bootstrap is its registered entry point name. Along with the
   658→        # bootstrap's name, a short message important to a user's choice can be shown
   659→        # also; for instance, several show "does not support iOS/Android deployment".
   660→        bootstrap_choices = {}
   661→        max_len = max(map(len, ordered))
   662→        for name, klass in ordered.items():
   663→            if annotation := getattr(klass, "display_name_annotation", ""):
   664→                annotation = f"{' ' * (max_len - len(name))} ({annotation})"
   665→            bootstrap_choices[f"{name}{annotation or ''}"] = klass
   666→
   667→        return bootstrap_choices

   701→    def parse_options(self, extra):
   702→        """Parse the command line arguments for the Command.

   705→        platform and format, a new ArgumentParser is created here to parse the remaining
   706→        command line arguments specific to the Command. Additionally, the default
   707→        options for disabling input, log verbosity, and log saving are parsed out and
   708→        saved to the Command.

   713→            configuration overrides.

   716→            get_platforms().get(self.platform), "DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT", None
   717→        )
   718→        # only show supported formats for Commands that support formats
   719→        if default_format is not None and self.command not in {"new", "dev", "upgrade"}:
   720→            formats = list(get_output_formats(self.platform).keys())
   721→            formats[formats.index(default_format)] = f"{default_format} (default)"
   722→            supported_formats_helptext = (
   723→                f"Supported formats:\n  {', '.join(sorted(formats, key=str.lower))}"
   724→            )
   725→        else:
   726→            supported_formats_helptext = ""
   727→
   728→        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   729→            prog=self.cmd_line.format(
   730→                command=self.command,
   731→                platform=self.platform,
   732→                output_format=self.output_format,
   733→            ),
   734→            description=self.input.textwrap(
   735→                f"{self.description}\n\n{supported_formats_helptext}"

   746→        # then process the argument list to strip out the passthrough args.
   747→        if self.allows_passthrough:
   748→            parser.add_argument(
   749→                "--",
   750→                dest="passthrough",
   751→                metavar="ARGS ...",
   752→                required=False,
   753→                help="Arguments to pass to the app",
   754→            )

   756→        else:
   757→            args = extra

   760→        # remaining after the basic command/platform/output format
   761→        # has been extracted.

   770→        self.logger.save_log = options.pop("save_log")
   771→

   773→        overrides = parse_config_overrides(options.pop("config_overrides"))

   934→    def update_cookiecutter_cache(self, template: str, branch="master"):

   936→
   937→        If the path is a local path, use the path as is.
   938→
   939→        If the path is a URL, look for a local cache; if one exists, update it,
   940→        including checking out the required branch.
   941→
   942→        :param template: The template URL or path.
   943→        :param branch: The template branch to use. Default: ``master``
   944→        :return: The path to the cached template. This may be the originally
   945→            provided path if the template was a file path.
   946→        """
   947→        if is_repo_url(template):
   948→            # The app template is a repository URL.
   949→            #
   950→            # Look for a Briefcase cache of the template.
   951→            cached_template = self.template_cache_path(template)
   952→
   953→            if cached_template.exists():
   954→                # There is a pre-existing cache of the template. Attempt to update it;
   955→                # if the fetch fails, use the existing state of the cache. Any other
   956→                # failure is surfaced to the user.
   957→                try:
   958→                    repo = self.tools.git.Repo(cached_template)
   959→                except self.tools.git.exc.GitError:
   960→                    # Template repository is in a weird state. Delete it
   961→                    self.logger.warning(
   962→                        "Template cache is in a weird state. Getting a clean clone."
   963→                    )
   964→                    self.tools.shutil.rmtree(cached_template)
   965→
   966→            if not cached_template.exists():
   967→                # There's no pre-existing template. It's either the first time seeing
   968→                # the template, or the template was in a weird state. Perform a blobless
   969→                # clone.
   970→                try:
   971→                    self.logger.info(f"Cloning template {template!r}...")
   972→                    cached_template.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
   973→                    repo = self.tools.git.Repo.clone_from(
   974→                        url=template,
   975→                        to_path=cached_template,
   976→                        filter=["blob:none"],
   977→                        no_checkout=True,
   978→                    )
   979→                except KeyboardInterrupt:
   980→                    # The user has aborted the initial clone. Git is fairly resilient to
   981→                    # being interrupted, but if the *initial* clone fails, it's very
   982→                    # hard to recover. To avoid problems on the next run, remove the
   983→                    # partial repo clone.
   984→                    if cached_template.exists():
   985→                        self.tools.shutil.rmtree(cached_template)
   986→                    raise
   987→                except self.tools.git.exc.GitError as e:
   988→                    # The clone failed; to make sure the repo is in a clean state, clean up
   989→                    # any partial remnants of this initial clone.
   990→                    # If we're getting a GitError, we know the directory must exist.
   991→                    self.tools.shutil.rmtree(cached_template)
   992→                    git_fatal_message = re.findall(r"(?<=fatal: ).*?$", e.stderr, re.S)
   993→                    if git_fatal_message:
   994→                        # GitError captures stderr with single quotes. Because the regex above
   995→                        # takes everything after git's "fatal" message, we need to strip that final single quote.
   996→                        hint = git_fatal_message[0].rstrip("'").strip()
   997→
   998→                        # git is inconsistent with capitalisation of the first word of the message
   999→                        # and about periods at the end of the message.
  1000→                        hint = f"{hint[0].upper()}{hint[1:]}{'' if hint[-1] == '.' else '.'}"
  1001→                    else:
  1002→                        hint = (
  1003→                            "This may be because your computer is offline, or "
  1004→                            "because the repository URL is incorrect."
  1005→                        )
  1006→
  1007→                    raise BriefcaseCommandError(
  1008→                        f"Unable to clone repository {template!r}.\n\n{hint}"
  1009→                    ) from e
  1010→
  1011→            try:
  1012→                # Raises ValueError if "origin" isn't a valid remote
  1013→                remote = repo.remote(name="origin")
  1014→                # Ensure the existing repo's origin URL points to the location
  1015→                # being requested. A difference can occur, for instance, if a
  1016→                # fork of the template is used.
  1017→                remote.set_url(new_url=template)
  1018→                try:
  1019→                    # Attempt to update the repository
  1020→                    remote.fetch()
  1021→                except self.tools.git.exc.GitCommandError as e:
  1022→                    # We are offline, or otherwise unable to contact the origin git
  1023→                    # repo. It's OK to continue; but capture the error in the log and

  1025→                    self.logger.debug(str(e))
  1026→                    self.logger.warning(
  1027→                        """
  1028→*************************************************************************
  1029→** WARNING: Unable to update template                                  **
  1030→*************************************************************************
  1031→
  1032→    Briefcase is unable the update the application template. This
  1033→    may be because your computer is currently offline. Briefcase will
  1034→    use existing template without updating.
  1035→
  1036→*************************************************************************
  1037→"""
  1038→                    )
  1039→
  1040→                try:
  1041→                    # Check out the branch for the required version tag.
  1042→                    head = remote.refs[branch]
  1043→
  1044→                    self.logger.info(
  1045→                        f"Using existing template (sha {head.commit.hexsha}, "
  1046→                        f"updated {head.commit.committed_datetime.strftime('%c')})"
  1047→                    )
  1048→                    head.checkout()
  1049→                except IndexError as e:

  1051→                    raise InvalidTemplateBranch(template, branch) from e
  1052→            except (ValueError, self.tools.git.exc.GitError) as e:
  1053→                raise BriefcaseCommandError(
  1054→                    "Unable to check out template branch.\n"
  1055→                    "\n"
  1056→                    "This may be because your computer is offline, or because the template repository\n"
  1057→                    "is in a weird state. If you have a stable network connection, try deleting:\n"
  1058→                    "\n"
  1059→                    f"    {cached_template}\n"
  1060→                    "\n"
  1061→                    "and retrying your command."
  1062→                ) from e

def build_gui_context(
        self,
        context: dict[str, str],
        project_overrides: dict[str, str],
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Build GUI context for convert, prompting for console app if needed.

        We must set the GUI framework to None here since the convert command uses the
        new command template. This template includes dependencies for GUI frameworks.
        For existing projects already configured with a GUI framework, those
        dependencies should already be listed. To prevent duplicate dependencies, we
        set the GUI framework to None here.

        Additionally, if the existing pyproject.toml does not already contain a
        console_app setting for the target app, prompt the user whether the app is a
        console app; if "Yes", inject console_app = true into the Briefcase app
        configuration via extra content for the cookiecutter template.
        """
        result: dict[str, str] = {"gui_framework": "None"}

        # Determine the app name from the context to check pyproject configuration.
        app_name = context.get("app_name")

        # If pyproject.toml already contains a console_app setting for this app,
        # skip prompting and don't add extra content.
        try:
            console_app_defined = (
                self.pyproject.get("tool", {})
                .get("briefcase", {})
                .get("app", {})
                .get(app_name, {})
                .get("console_app")
                is not None
            )
        except AttributeError:
            # If pyproject isn't a mapping for some reason, treat as undefined.
            console_app_defined = False

        if console_app_defined:
            self.logger.info(
                f"Existing pyproject.toml contains a console_app setting for app {app_name!r}; skipping console prompt."
            )
            return result

        # Prompt the user to determine if the app is a console app. Default to "No".
        # Do not mutate project_overrides; only use any provided 'console_app' override if present.
        override_value = None
        if isinstance(project_overrides, dict):
            ov = project_overrides.get("console_app")
            # Accept only explicit "Yes" or "No" overrides.
            if ov in {"Yes", "No"}:
                override_value = ov

        answer = self.select_option(
            intro=(
                "Is your existing application a console app?\n\n"
                "Selecting 'Yes' will configure Briefcase to run the app in a terminal."
            ),
            variable="Console App",
            default="No",
            options=["No", "Yes"],
            override_value=override_value,
        )

        if answer == "Yes":
            # Inject additional content into [tool.briefcase.app.<app_name>] table.
            # Ensure a trailing newline, and avoid duplicates (handled by template merge).
            result["pyproject_table_briefcase_app_extra_content"] = "console_app = true\n"

        return result

   206→    @contextmanager
   207→    def context(self, context: str):
   208→        """Wrap a collection of output in a logging context.
   209→
   210→        A logging context is a prefix on every logging line. It is used when a set of
   211→        commands (and output) is being run in a very specific way that needs to be
   212→        highlighted, such as running a command in a Docker container.

   215→            with no markup or other special characters.

   219→        old_context = self._context
   220→        self._context = f"{context}| "
   221→        self.info("-" * (72 - len(context)))
   222→        try:
   223→            yield
   224→        finally:
   225→            self.info("-" * (72 - len(context)))
   226→            self._context = old_context
   227→            self.info(f"Leaving {context} context.")

   230→    def _log(

   237→        style=None,

   240→
   241→        :param preface: value to be printed on the far left of the message and symbolic
   242→            of the type of message being printed.

   244→            presented as dimmer compared to the styling of the message text.

   569→    @contextmanager
   570→    def wait_bar(
   571→        self,
   572→        message: str = "",
   573→        done_message: str = "done",
   574→        *,
   575→        transient: bool = False,
   576→        markup: bool = False,
   577→    ) -> NotDeadYet:
   578→        """Activates the Wait Bar as a context manager.
   579→
   580→        If the Wait Bar is already active, then its message is updated for the new
   581→        context. Once the new context is complete, the previous Wait Bar message
   582→        is restored.
   583→
   584→        :param message: text explaining what is being awaited; should end in '...'
   585→        :param done_message: text appended to the message after exiting
   586→        :param transient: if True, remove bar and message from screen after exiting;
   587→            if False (default), the message will remain on the screen without pulsing bar.
   588→        :param markup: whether to interpret Rich styling markup in the message; if True,
   589→            the message must already be escaped; defaults False.
   590→        :returns:  Keep-alive spinner to notify user Briefcase is still waiting
   591→        """
   592→        is_wait_bar_disabled = not self.is_interactive
   593→        show_outcome_message = message and (is_wait_bar_disabled or not transient)
   594→
   595→        if self._wait_bar is None:
   596→            self._wait_bar = Progress(
   597→                TextColumn("    "),
   598→                BarColumn(bar_width=20, style="black", pulse_style="white"),
   599→                TextColumn("{task.fields[message]}"),
   600→                transient=True,
   601→                disable=is_wait_bar_disabled,
   602→                console=self.print.console,
   603→            )
   604→            # start=False causes the progress bar to "pulse"
   605→            # message=None is a sentinel the Wait Bar should be inactive
   606→            self._wait_bar.add_task("", start=False, message=None)
   607→
   608→        self.print(
   609→            f"{message} started", markup=markup, show=message and is_wait_bar_disabled
   610→        )
   611→
   612→        self.is_console_controlled = True
   613→        wait_bar_task = self._wait_bar.tasks[0]
   614→        previous_message = wait_bar_task.fields["message"]
   615→        self._wait_bar.update(wait_bar_task.id, message=message)
   616→
   617→        try:
   618→            self._wait_bar.start()
   619→            yield NotDeadYet(printer=self.print)
   620→        except BaseException as e:
   621→            # capture BaseException so message is left on the screen even if user sends CTRL+C
   622→            error_message = "aborted" if isinstance(e, KeyboardInterrupt) else "errored"
   623→            self.print(
   624→                f"{message} {error_message}", markup=markup, show=show_outcome_message
   625→            )
   626→            raise
   627→        else:
   628→            self.print(
   629→                f"{message} {done_message}", markup=markup, show=show_outcome_message
   630→            )
   631→        finally:
   632→            self._wait_bar.update(wait_bar_task.id, message=previous_message)
   633→            # Deactivate the Wait Bar if returning to its initial state
   634→            if previous_message is None:
   635→                self._wait_bar.stop()
   636→                self.is_console_controlled = False

   643→        process is interrupted or a user needs to be prompted. For instance, when batch
   644→        scripts are interrupted by CTRL+C in cmd.exe, the user may be prompted to abort

   646→        prompt may be hidden from the user.

   439→    def get_license_from_text(self, license_text: str) -> str:
   440→        """Infer the license from the license file."""
   441→        # The order here is quite important. If we have GPLvX+ after GPLvX, then it will
   442→        # never be matched if the license text is GPLvX+, since it will already have
   443→        # matched GPLvX. We search for MIT last, because words like PERMITTED and
   444→        # LIMITED will generate a false match.
   445→
   446→        hint_patterns = {
   447→            "Apache Software License": ["Apache"],
   448→            "BSD license": [
   449→                "Redistribution and use in source and binary forms",
   450→                "BSD",
   451→            ],
   452→            "GNU General Public License v2 or later (GPLv2+)": [
   453→                "Free Software Foundation, either version 2 of the License",
   454→                "GPLv2+",
   455→            ],
   456→            "GNU General Public License v2 (GPLv2)": [
   457→                "version 2 of the GNU General Public License",
   458→                "GPLv2",
   459→            ],
   460→            "GNU General Public License v3 or later (GPLv3+)": [
   461→                "either version 3 of the License",
   462→                "GPLv3+",
   463→            ],
   464→            "GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3)": [
   465→                "version 3 of the GNU General Public License",
   466→                "GPLv3",
   467→            ],
   468→            "MIT license": [
   469→                "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge",
   470→                "MIT",
   471→            ],
   472→        }
   473→        for hint, license_patterns in hint_patterns.items():
   474→            for license_pattern in license_patterns:
   475→                if license_pattern.lower() in license_text.lower():
   476→                    return hint
   477→
   478→        return "Other"

   596→    def build_gui_context(

   598→        context: dict[str, str],
   599→        project_overrides: dict[str, str],
   600→    ) -> dict[str, str]:
   601→        """Build GUI context for convert, prompting for console app if needed.
   602→
   603→        We must set the GUI framework to None here since the convert command uses the
   604→        new command template. This template includes dependencies for GUI frameworks.
   605→        For existing projects already configured with a GUI framework, those
   606→        dependencies should already be listed. To prevent duplicate dependencies, we
   607→        set the GUI framework to None here.
   608→
   609→        Additionally, if the existing pyproject.toml does not already contain a
   610→        console_app setting for the target app, prompt the user whether the app is a
   611→        console app; if "Yes", inject console_app = true into the Briefcase app
   612→        configuration via extra content for the cookiecutter template.
   613→        """
   614→        result: dict[str, str] = {"gui_framework": "None"}
   615→
   616→        # Determine the app name from the context to check pyproject configuration.
   617→        app_name = context.get("app_name")
   618→
   619→        # If pyproject.toml already contains a console_app setting for this app,
   620→        # skip prompting and don't add extra content.
   621→        try:
   622→            console_app_defined = (
   623→                self.pyproject.get("tool", {})
   624→                .get("briefcase", {})
   625→                .get("app", {})
   626→                .get(app_name, {})
   627→                .get("console_app")
   628→                is not None
   629→            )
   630→        except AttributeError:
   631→            # If pyproject isn't a mapping for some reason, treat as undefined.
   632→            console_app_defined = False
   633→
   634→        if console_app_defined:
   635→            self.logger.info(
   636→                f"Existing pyproject.toml contains a console_app setting for app {app_name!r}; skipping console prompt."
   637→            )
   638→            return result
   639→
   640→        # Prompt the user to determine if the app is a console app. Default to "No".
   641→        # Do not mutate project_overrides; only use any provided 'console_app' override if present.
   642→        override_value = None
   643→        if isinstance(project_overrides, dict):
   644→            ov = project_overrides.get("console_app")
   645→            # Accept only explicit "Yes" or "No" overrides.
   646→            if ov in {"Yes", "No"}:
   647→                override_value = ov
   648→
   649→        answer = self.select_option(
   650→            intro=(
   651→                "Is your existing application a console app?\n\n"
   652→                "Selecting 'Yes' will configure Briefcase to run the app in a terminal."
   653→            ),
